```{r}
# ============================================================
# starter_score.R
# Scores a team's starting pitchers for playoff series prediction.
#
# xFIP              60%  - overall quality (HR/K/BB), primary metric
# Stamina           10%  - pitches per start
# TTO3 wOBA-against 15%  - proxy for degradation 3rd time through
#                          (xFIP itself isn't split by TTO -- this
#                          comes from a manually-maintained CSV since
#                          FanGraphs' TTO splits live in a separate
#                          tool baseballr doesn't wrap. Shrunk toward
#                          league average based on batters faced.)
# IFFB%              5%  - infield fly ball rate: weak/mistimed contact
# Non-pulled batted%  5%  - Cent_pct + Oppo_pct, proxy for "not pulled"
#                          (FanGraphs doesn't split FB-specific pull rate,
#                          so this uses all-batted-ball direction as the
#                          nearest available proxy)
# Soft contact %      5%  - Soft_pct from FanGraphs batted-ball profile
#
# IFFB%, non-pulled%, and Soft% are all shrunk toward the league
# average based on TBF (total batters faced), so pitchers with thin
# samples (injuries, midseason call-ups, low-volume guys like a
# Blake Snell type) don't get over/under-rated by noise.
#
# NOTE: fg_pitcher_leaders() returns ALL stat categories in one call
# in current baseballr versions -- xFIP, IFFB_pct, Cent_pct, Oppo_pct,
# Soft_pct, and TBF all come back together, so there's no need for a
# separate "batted ball" call.
#
# Requires: baseballr, dplyr
# ============================================================

library(baseballr)
library(dplyr)

# ---- Config: tune these weights as we go -------------------
STARTER_WEIGHTS <- list(
  xfip          = 0.60,  # primary: overall quality
  stamina       = 0.10,  # pitches per start
  tto3_penalty  = 0.15,  # wOBA-against 3rd time through, inverted
  iffb          = 0.05,  # infield fly ball rate
  non_pulled    = 0.05,  # Cent_pct + Oppo_pct, proxy for non-pulled contact
  soft_contact  = 0.05   # Soft_pct from batted-ball profile
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Season xFIP, stamina, and batted-ball profile -- all in
#    one fg_pitcher_leaders() call for all qualified starters.
#    IFFB%, non-pulled%, and Soft% are shrunk toward league
#    average based on TBF (sample size) before being returned.
# ------------------------------------------------------------
get_pitcher_base_stats <- function(season, teams = NULL,
                                    name_lookup_path = "team_name_lookup.csv",
                                    k_batted_ball = 150) {
  fg <- fg_pitcher_leaders(
    startseason = season,
    endseason   = season,
    qual        = "0",
    stats       = "sta", # starters (was `pitcher_type` in older baseballr versions)
    ind         = 1      # split traded pitchers by team-stint instead of aggregating
  )

  # League-wide averages computed BEFORE filtering to specific teams,
  # so the shrinkage baseline reflects the full league, not a small
  # biased subset. Confirm `TBF` is the exact column name in your
  # baseballr version with names(fg) -- it may be spelled differently.
  league_avg_iffb       <- mean(fg$IFFB_pct, na.rm = TRUE)
  league_avg_soft       <- mean(fg$Soft_pct, na.rm = TRUE)
  league_avg_non_pulled <- mean(fg$Cent_pct + fg$Oppo_pct, na.rm = TRUE)

  result <- fg %>%
    transmute(
      player_name    = PlayerName,
      team           = team_name,
      xFIP           = xFIP,
      pitches        = Pitches,
      GS             = GS,
      G              = G,
      TBF            = TBF,  # <-- confirm this column name with names(fg)
      pitches_per_start  = Pitches / GS,
      iffb_pct_raw       = IFFB_pct,
      non_pulled_pct_raw = Cent_pct + Oppo_pct,
      soft_pct_raw       = Soft_pct
    ) %>%
    # Safety net: regardless of whether the server-side `stats = "sta"`
    # filter behaved as expected, only keep pitchers who were actually
    # used as starters this season (most of their appearances were starts).
    filter(GS > 0, GS / G >= 0.5) %>%
    # FanGraphs sometimes returns a dash placeholder like "- - -" instead
    # of a real blank/NA when a player's team is ambiguous under the
    # ind=1 split. Convert that to a real NA so the lookup-patch below
    # actually catches it. (Detects "no letters/digits" rather than
    # matching specific dash characters, since those can vary.)
    mutate(team = ifelse(grepl("[A-Za-z0-9]", team), team, NA)) %>%
    # Shrink thin-sample batted-ball rates toward league average,
    # weighted by TBF -- keeps low-volume pitchers (injuries, limited
    # innings) from swinging the composite score off noise.
    mutate(
      iffb_pct       = (TBF * iffb_pct_raw + k_batted_ball * league_avg_iffb) / (TBF + k_batted_ball),
      non_pulled_pct = (TBF * non_pulled_pct_raw + k_batted_ball * league_avg_non_pulled) / (TBF + k_batted_ball),
      soft_pct       = (TBF * soft_pct_raw + k_batted_ball * league_avg_soft) / (TBF + k_batted_ball)
    )

  # Patch in missing team labels for traded pitchers -- their stats from
  # the ind=1 split are already correct, only the team name came back blank.
  # See team_name_lookup.csv (columns: player_name, team).
  if (file.exists(name_lookup_path)) {
    lookup <- read.csv(name_lookup_path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE) %>%
      mutate(player_name = trimws(player_name))
    result <- result %>%
      mutate(player_name = trimws(player_name)) %>%
      left_join(lookup, by = "player_name", suffix = c("", "_lookup")) %>%
      mutate(team = ifelse(is.na(team), team_lookup, team)) %>%
      select(-team_lookup)
  }

  if (!is.null(teams)) {
    result <- result %>% filter(team %in% teams)
  }

  result
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. wOBA-against by times-through-the-order (3rd time)
#    FanGraphs' TTO splits live behind their separate Splits Tool,
#    which baseballr doesn't currently wrap. Instead, this reads a
#    small manually-maintained CSV -- only the playoff teams' top
#    3-4 starters ever need this, so it's a short list to keep
#    updated each postseason. See tto3_lookup.csv for the expected
#    format (player_name, team, woba_tto3, bf_tto3).
#
#    The raw wOBA is shrunk toward a league-average baseline,
#    weighted by bf_tto3 (batters faced 3rd time through), so
#    low-volume pitchers (e.g. a Blake Snell type who doesn't
#    rack up innings) don't get an unreliable score from a thin
#    sample -- good or bad.
# ------------------------------------------------------------
get_tto3_woba <- function(lookup_path = "tto3_lookup.csv", k = 60, league_avg_woba = 0.335) {
  raw <- read.csv(lookup_path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

  raw %>%
    mutate(
      woba_tto3 = (bf_tto3 * woba_tto3 + k * league_avg_woba) / (bf_tto3 + k)
    )
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Normalize a stat to a 0-1 scale within the season's pool
#    (lower-is-better stats get inverted so 1 = best)
# ------------------------------------------------------------
normalize <- function(x, lower_is_better = FALSE) {  # all calls here pass it explicitly
  r <- range(x, na.rm = TRUE)
  scaled <- (x - r[1]) / (r[2] - r[1])
  if (lower_is_better) 1 - scaled else scaled
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Build a single composite score per pitcher
# ------------------------------------------------------------
build_starter_scores <- function(season, teams = NULL, tto3_path = "tto3_lookup.csv") {
  base <- get_pitcher_base_stats(season, teams = teams)
  tto3 <- get_tto3_woba(tto3_path)

  combined <- base %>%
    left_join(tto3, by = c("player_name", "team")) %>%
    mutate(
      xfip_score       = normalize(xFIP, lower_is_better = TRUE),
      stamina_score    = normalize(pitches_per_start, lower_is_better = FALSE),
      tto3_score       = normalize(woba_tto3, lower_is_better = TRUE),
      iffb_score       = normalize(iffb_pct, lower_is_better = FALSE),   # more IFFB% = better
      non_pulled_score = normalize(non_pulled_pct, lower_is_better = FALSE),
      soft_score       = normalize(soft_pct, lower_is_better = FALSE),  # more soft contact = better
      composite = STARTER_WEIGHTS$xfip * xfip_score +
                  STARTER_WEIGHTS$stamina * stamina_score +
                  STARTER_WEIGHTS$tto3_penalty * tto3_score +
                  STARTER_WEIGHTS$iffb * iffb_score +
                  STARTER_WEIGHTS$non_pulled * non_pulled_score +
                  STARTER_WEIGHTS$soft_contact * soft_score
    )

  combined
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Get a team's top-N starters by composite score, in order
#    (used differently per round: WC uses top 3, DS/CS/WS use top 4).
#
#    By default this just ranks by composite. To force the result
#    to only the pitchers you actually expect in the rotation
#    (e.g. excluding a small-sample call-up who scores artificially
#    high), either:
#      - pass only_players = c("Name1", "Name2", ...) for a quick
#        one-off override, or
#      - maintain a confirmed_rotation.csv (columns: team, player_name)
#        listing your intended starters per team; if present, it's
#        used automatically for any team it covers.
#    Either way, the players who make the cut are still ranked by
#    composite among themselves, so the ordering (Game 1 starter vs.
#    Game 4 starter) stays data-driven.
# ------------------------------------------------------------
get_team_rotation <- function(scores_df, team_abbr, n = 4,
                               only_players = NULL,
                               confirmed_path = "confirmed_rotation.csv") {
  df <- scores_df %>% filter(team == team_abbr)

  if (!is.null(only_players)) {
    df <- df %>% filter(player_name %in% only_players)
  } else if (file.exists(confirmed_path)) {
    confirmed <- read.csv(confirmed_path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE) %>%
      filter(team == team_abbr) %>%
      pull(player_name)
    if (length(confirmed) > 0) {
      df <- df %>% filter(player_name %in% confirmed)
    }
  }

  df %>%
    arrange(desc(composite)) %>%
    slice_head(n = n)
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Example usage:
# scores <- build_starter_scores(2026, teams = c("PHI", "LAD", "MIL", "NYM"))
# get_team_rotation(scores, "PHI", n = 4)
# get_team_rotation(scores, "PHI", n = 4, only_players = c("Zack Wheeler", "Cristopher Sánchez"))
# ------------------------------------------------------------
```


```{r}
# ============================================================
# team_defense_score.R
# Team defense score: 50% DRS (FanGraphs/SIS) + 50% FRV (Statcast).
# No separate arm bucket -- already inside both metrics.
#
# Inputs: team_frv_lookup.csv (col: name, total_runs)
#         team_drs_lookup.csv (col: Team, DRS)
# Both use team abbreviations directly.
# ============================================================

library(dplyr)

get_team_frv <- function(path = "team_frv_lookup.csv") {
  read.csv(path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE) %>%
    transmute(team = toupper(trimws(name)), team_frv = total_runs)
}

get_team_drs <- function(path = "team_drs_lookup.csv") {
  read.csv(path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE) %>%
    transmute(team = toupper(trimws(Team)), team_drs = DRS)
}

normalize <- function(x, lower_is_better = FALSE) {
  r <- range(x, na.rm = TRUE)
  s <- (x - r[1]) / (r[2] - r[1])
  if (lower_is_better) 1 - s else s
}

build_team_defense_scores <- function(teams = NULL,
                                       frv_path = "team_frv_lookup.csv",
                                       drs_path = "team_drs_lookup.csv") {
  frv <- get_team_frv(frv_path)
  drs <- get_team_drs(drs_path)

  combined <- frv %>%
    full_join(drs, by = "team") %>%
    mutate(
      frv_score = normalize(team_frv),
      drs_score = normalize(team_drs),
      composite = 0.5 * frv_score + 0.5 * drs_score
    )

  if (!is.null(teams)) combined <- combined %>% filter(team %in% teams)
  combined %>% arrange(desc(composite))
}

# defense <- build_team_defense_scores(teams = c("PHI","LAD","MIL", ...))

```

```{r}
# ============================================================
# lineup_score.R
# Scores a team's expected lineup for playoff series prediction.
#
# wRC+          40%  - season, park/league-adjusted overall production
# xwOBA         40%  - season, Statcast contact-quality (luck-stripped)
# 2nd-half      15%  - blend of 2nd-half wRC+ and 2nd-half xwOBA (7.5/7.5)
# Baserunning    5%  - Statcast baserunning run value
#
# Only players listed in expected_lineup.csv (team, player_name) are
# scored -- this is how injuries/bench decisions get handled, same
# pattern as confirmed_rotation.csv for starters.
#
# wRC+ is pulled programmatically via fg_batter_leaders() (like xFIP
# was for starters). xwOBA and baserunning are read from manually
# exported Baseball Savant CSVs -- same reasoning as team defense:
# baseballr's Statcast wrapper functions proved unreliable to guess,
# so CSV export is the more robust path for Statcast-flavored stats.
#
# Requires: baseballr, dplyr
# ============================================================

library(baseballr)
library(dplyr)

LINEUP_WEIGHTS <- list(
  wrc_plus     = 0.40,
  xwoba        = 0.40,
  second_half  = 0.15,  # split 7.5/7.5 between 2H wRC+ and 2H xwOBA
  baserunning  = 0.05
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Name normalization -- same defensive pattern as starter_score.R
# (handles case differences and encoding issues like Rodon/deGrom).
# ------------------------------------------------------------
normalize_name <- function(x) {
  x <- iconv(x, to = "UTF-8", sub = "byte")
  x <- tolower(trimws(x))
  # Manual diacritic strip instead of iconv(..., to = "ASCII//TRANSLIT"):
  # that TRANSLIT step is unreliable on Windows (drops/mangles accented
  # characters instead of cleanly stripping them), which is almost
  # certainly why accented names weren't matching plain-ASCII ones in
  # expected_lineup.csv. chartr() is deterministic on any OS.
  from <- "áàäâãåéèëêíìïîóòöôõøúùüûñçýÿ"
  to   <- "aaaaaaeeeeiiiioooooouuuuncyy"
  chartr(from, to, x)
}

normalize <- function(x, lower_is_better = FALSE) {
  r <- range(x, na.rm = TRUE)
  s <- (x - r[1]) / (r[2] - r[1])
  if (lower_is_better) 1 - s else s
}

# Different sources abbreviate the same team differently (Savant's
# baserunning leaderboard uses TB/SD, FanGraphs uses TBR/SDP, etc.).
# Canonicalize to the FanGraphs-style codes -- whatever you used in
# expected_lineup.csv -- so team-based joins don't silently miss.
TEAM_ALIASES <- c(
  "TB" = "TBR", "SD" = "SDP", "CWS" = "CHW", "WSH" = "WSN",
  "KC" = "KCR", "SF" = "SFG", "AZ" = "ARI"
)
normalize_team <- function(x) {
  x <- toupper(trimws(x))
  ifelse(x %in% names(TEAM_ALIASES), TEAM_ALIASES[x], x)
}

# Savant exports name players as "Last, First" in a column literally
# called `last_name, first_name`. Flip it to "First Last" so it lines
# up with normalize_name() applied to FanGraphs' PlayerName elsewhere.
savant_name_to_join <- function(x) {
  flipped <- sub("^(.*), (.*)$", "\\2 \\1", x)
  normalize_name(flipped)
}

# Savant CSVs can carry blank/duplicate header cells (from merged export
# headers) that read.csv(check.names = FALSE) preserves as literal NA/""
# column names -- those break dplyr verbs. Drop them before use.
drop_unnamed_cols <- function(df) {
  df[, !is.na(names(df)) & names(df) != "", drop = FALSE]
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Expected lineup -- the master list of who actually gets scored
# ------------------------------------------------------------
get_expected_lineup <- function(path = "expected_lineup.csv") {
  read.csv(path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE) %>%
    mutate(join_name = normalize_name(player_name),
           team = normalize_team(team))
}

# Same dash-placeholder patch as starter_score.R: a traded player's row
# sometimes comes back with team = "- - -" (ind=1 stint split) or
# "2 Tms" (combined, non-split) instead of a real abbreviation. Convert
# either to real NA, then patch from team_name_lookup.csv (columns:
# player_name, team) -- same file the pitcher module uses.
patch_traded_team <- function(df, name_lookup_path = "team_name_lookup.csv") {
  df <- df %>%
    mutate(team = ifelse(!grepl("[A-Za-z0-9]", team) | grepl("Tms", team, ignore.case = TRUE),
                          NA, team))

  if (file.exists(name_lookup_path)) {
    lookup <- read.csv(name_lookup_path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE) %>%
      mutate(join_name = normalize_name(player_name)) %>%
      select(join_name, team_lookup = team)
    df <- df %>%
      left_join(lookup, by = "join_name") %>%
      mutate(team = ifelse(is.na(team), team_lookup, team)) %>%
      select(-team_lookup)
  }
  df
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Season wRC+ via FanGraphs
#    ind = 0 (default, no team split) -- for a traded player, this
#    gives one combined full-season row instead of two partial ones,
#    since we want their whole season, not just the current-team slice
#    (2nd-half numbers below still capture the recent-team picture).
# ------------------------------------------------------------
#    Shrunk toward league average, weighted by PA, k = 150 -- same
#    reasoning as xwOBA's shrinkage.
get_batter_wrc <- function(season, k = 150) {
  fg <- fg_batter_leaders(
    startseason = season,
    endseason   = season,
    qual        = "0",
    stats       = "bat"
  )

  league_avg_wrc <- mean(fg$wRC_plus, na.rm = TRUE)

  fg %>%
    transmute(
      join_name    = normalize_name(PlayerName),
      team         = normalize_team(team_name),
      wrc_plus_raw = wRC_plus,
      pa           = PA,
      wrc_plus     = (pa * wrc_plus_raw + k * league_avg_wrc) / (pa + k)
    ) %>%
    select(join_name, team, wrc_plus) %>%
    patch_traded_team()
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. 2nd-half wRC+ via FanGraphs date range
#    Adjust start_date each season -- rough All-Star-break proxy.
# ------------------------------------------------------------
get_batter_wrc_2h <- function(season, start_date, end_date) {
  fg <- fg_batter_leaders(
    startseason = season,
    endseason   = season,
    qual        = "0",
    stats       = "bat",
    month       = "1000",  # sentinel: tells FanGraphs to honor startdate/enddate
    startdate   = start_date,
    enddate     = end_date,
    ind         = 1
  )

  fg %>%
    transmute(
      join_name    = normalize_name(PlayerName),
      team         = normalize_team(team_name),
      wrc_plus_2h  = wRC_plus
    ) %>%
    patch_traded_team()
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Season xwOBA -- Baseball Savant CSV export
#    Shrunk toward league average, weighted by PA, k = 150 (roughly
#    where xwOBA stabilizes) so low-PA guys don't get extreme scores
#    off a thin sample.
# ------------------------------------------------------------
get_batter_xwoba <- function(path = "team_xwoba_lookup.csv", k = 150, league_avg_xwoba = NULL) {
  raw <- read.csv(path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE, check.names = FALSE) %>%
    drop_unnamed_cols()

  if (is.null(league_avg_xwoba)) {
    league_avg_xwoba <- mean(raw$est_woba, na.rm = TRUE)
  }

  raw %>%
    transmute(
      join_name  = savant_name_to_join(`last_name, first_name`),
      xwoba_raw  = est_woba,
      pa         = pa,
      xwoba      = (pa * xwoba_raw + k * league_avg_xwoba) / (pa + k)
    ) %>%
    select(join_name, xwoba)
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. 2nd-half xwOBA -- Savant export filtered to 2nd half before export
#    No shrinkage here -- no strong stabilization-point argument for
#    a half-season split the way there is for full-season xwOBA/wRC+.
# ------------------------------------------------------------
get_batter_xwoba_2h <- function(path = "team_xwoba_2h_lookup.csv") {
  # This export uses a different layout than the season file: plain
  # "player_name" (already First Last) and "xwOBA" (capitalized).
  read.csv(path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE, check.names = FALSE) %>%
    drop_unnamed_cols() %>%
    transmute(
      join_name = normalize_name(player_name),
      team      = normalize_team(team),
      xwoba_2h  = xwOBA
    ) %>%
    patch_traded_team()
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Baserunning run value -- Savant export
#    <-- CONFIRM stat column name (name column assumed same "Last, First" format)
# ------------------------------------------------------------
get_baserunning <- function(path = "team_baserunning_lookup.csv") {
  read.csv(path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE, check.names = FALSE) %>%
    drop_unnamed_cols() %>%
    transmute(
      # This export uses `entity_name`, not `last_name, first_name` --
      # check its format (Last, First vs First Last) and swap
      # savant_name_to_join() for normalize_name() below if it's
      # already "First Last".
      join_name = savant_name_to_join(entity_name),
      team      = normalize_team(team_name),
      baserunning_runs = runner_runs_tot
    )
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 7. Build composite lineup scores
# ------------------------------------------------------------
build_lineup_scores <- function(season, start_date_2h, end_date_2h,
                                 lineup_path = "expected_lineup.csv",
                                 xwoba_path = "team_xwoba_lookup.csv",
                                 xwoba_2h_path = "team_xwoba_2h_lookup.csv",
                                 baserunning_path = "team_baserunning_lookup.csv") {

  lineup    <- get_expected_lineup(lineup_path)
  wrc       <- get_batter_wrc(season)
  wrc_2h    <- get_batter_wrc_2h(season, start_date_2h, end_date_2h)
  xwoba     <- get_batter_xwoba(xwoba_path)
  xwoba_2h  <- get_batter_xwoba_2h(xwoba_2h_path)
  baserun   <- get_baserunning(baserunning_path)

  # Join on team + join_name, not join_name alone -- there are real
  # same-name collisions in MLB (two different Max Muncys), and joining
  # on name only lets one lineup row match multiple FanGraphs rows,
  # duplicating it and scrambling which stats land on which player.
  combined <- lineup %>%
    left_join(wrc,      by = c("join_name", "team")) %>%
    left_join(wrc_2h,   by = c("join_name", "team")) %>%
    left_join(xwoba,     by = "join_name") %>%  # season xwOBA export has no team col
    left_join(xwoba_2h,  by = c("join_name", "team")) %>%
    left_join(baserun,   by = c("join_name", "team")) %>%
    mutate(
      wrc_score      = normalize(wrc_plus),
      xwoba_score    = normalize(xwoba),
      wrc_2h_score   = normalize(wrc_plus_2h),
      xwoba_2h_score = normalize(xwoba_2h),
      second_half_score = (wrc_2h_score + xwoba_2h_score) / 2,
      baserunning_score = normalize(baserunning_runs),

      # Guys with no 2nd-half PAs (e.g. injured all 2nd half) get NA here,
      # which would otherwise NA out the whole composite. Instead: drop
      # the 2nd-half term and rescale the remaining weights up so they
      # still sum to 1 -- their score is then based purely on the other
      # components, not artificially docked for missing data.
      composite = ifelse(
        is.na(second_half_score),
        (LINEUP_WEIGHTS$wrc_plus * wrc_score +
           LINEUP_WEIGHTS$xwoba * xwoba_score +
           LINEUP_WEIGHTS$baserunning * baserunning_score) /
          (1 - LINEUP_WEIGHTS$second_half),
        LINEUP_WEIGHTS$wrc_plus * wrc_score +
          LINEUP_WEIGHTS$xwoba * xwoba_score +
          LINEUP_WEIGHTS$second_half * second_half_score +
          LINEUP_WEIGHTS$baserunning * baserunning_score
      )
    )

  combined %>% arrange(team, desc(composite))
}
```

```{r}
# ============================================================
# bullpen_score.R
# Scores each team's expected bullpen (incl. starters used in relief)
# using 1st-time-through-the-order (TTO1) stats for everyone.
#
# K-BB%          60%  - stuff + control, stabilizes fastest
# HR/9           15%  - lower is better
# wOBA-against   15%  - lower is better
# 2nd half       10%  - same three stats (TTO1, 2nd half only), mixed
#                       60/20/20 internally; no shrinkage
#
# Inputs:
#   tto1_lookup.csv       - FanGraphs Splits Tool export, TTO1 split,
#                           ALL pitchers (full pool = real league avg
#                           for shrinkage)
#   tto1_2h_lookup.csv    - same export, date range set to 2nd half
#   expected_bullpen.csv - team, player_name (~7 per team, your picks)
#
# Season stats are shrunk toward league average by batters faced,
# since reliever samples are thin. If a pitcher has no 2nd-half data,
# the 2nd-half weight is dropped and the rest rescaled (same as lineup).
# ============================================================

library(dplyr)

BULLPEN_WEIGHTS <- list(k_bb = 0.60, hr = 0.15, woba = 0.15, second_half = 0.10)
WEIGHTS_2H_INNER <- list(k_bb = 0.60, hr = 0.20, woba = 0.20)

normalize_name <- function(x) {
  x <- iconv(x, to = "UTF-8", sub = "byte")
  x <- tolower(trimws(x))
  from <- "áàäâãåéèëêíìïîóòöôõøúùüûñçýÿ"
  to   <- "aaaaaaeeeeiiiioooooouuuuncyy"
  chartr(from, to, x)
}

TEAM_ALIASES <- c("TB" = "TBR", "SD" = "SDP", "CWS" = "CHW", "WSH" = "WSN",
                  "KC" = "KCR", "SF" = "SFG", "AZ" = "ARI")
normalize_team <- function(x) {
  x <- toupper(trimws(x))
  ifelse(x %in% names(TEAM_ALIASES), TEAM_ALIASES[x], x)
}

# FanGraphs exports can store percentages as text ("25.3 %")
to_num <- function(x) as.numeric(gsub("[% ,]", "", as.character(x)))

normalize <- function(x, lower_is_better = FALSE) {
  r <- range(x, na.rm = TRUE)
  s <- (x - r[1]) / (r[2] - r[1])
  if (lower_is_better) 1 - s else s
}

shrink <- function(raw, n, league_avg, k) (n * raw + k * league_avg) / (n + k)

# Exports can carry blank header cells -> NA/"" column names, which
# break dplyr. Drop them (same fix as lineup_score.R).
drop_unnamed_cols <- function(df) {
  df[, !is.na(names(df)) & names(df) != "", drop = FALSE]
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. TTO1 stats for all pitchers, shrunk by BF
#    Columns: player_name, team, IP, TBF, wOBA, HR/9, K-BB%
# ------------------------------------------------------------
get_tto1_stats <- function(path = "tto1_lookup.csv",
                           k_kbb = 100, k_hr = 300, k_woba = 200) {
  raw <- read.csv(path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE, check.names = FALSE) %>%
    drop_unnamed_cols() %>%
    transmute(
      join_name = normalize_name(player_name),
      bf        = to_num(TBF),
      k_bb_raw  = to_num(`K-BB%`),
      hr_raw    = to_num(`HR/9`),
      woba_raw  = to_num(wOBA)
    )

  raw %>%
    mutate(
      k_bb = shrink(k_bb_raw, bf, mean(k_bb_raw, na.rm = TRUE), k_kbb),
      hr   = shrink(hr_raw,   bf, mean(hr_raw,   na.rm = TRUE), k_hr),
      woba = shrink(woba_raw, bf, mean(woba_raw, na.rm = TRUE), k_woba)
    )
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 1b. 2nd-half TTO1 stats -- raw, no shrinkage
# ------------------------------------------------------------
get_tto1_2h_stats <- function(path = "tto1_2h_lookup.csv") {
  read.csv(path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE, check.names = FALSE) %>%
    drop_unnamed_cols() %>%
    transmute(
      join_name = normalize_name(player_name),
      k_bb_2h   = to_num(`K-BB%`),
      hr_2h     = to_num(`HR/9`),
      woba_2h   = to_num(wOBA)
    )
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Per-pitcher scores for your confirmed bullpens
# ------------------------------------------------------------
build_bullpen_scores <- function(tto1_path = "tto1_lookup.csv",
                                 tto1_2h_path = "tto1_2h_lookup.csv",
                                 bullpen_path = "expected_bullpen.csv") {
  pen  <- read.csv(bullpen_path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE) %>%
    mutate(join_name = normalize_name(player_name),
           team      = normalize_team(team))
  tto1    <- get_tto1_stats(tto1_path)
  tto1_2h <- get_tto1_2h_stats(tto1_2h_path)

  pen %>%
    left_join(tto1,    by = "join_name") %>%
    left_join(tto1_2h, by = "join_name") %>%
    mutate(
      k_bb_score = normalize(k_bb),
      hr_score   = normalize(hr,   lower_is_better = TRUE),
      woba_score = normalize(woba, lower_is_better = TRUE),

      second_half_score =
        WEIGHTS_2H_INNER$k_bb * normalize(k_bb_2h) +
        WEIGHTS_2H_INNER$hr   * normalize(hr_2h,   lower_is_better = TRUE) +
        WEIGHTS_2H_INNER$woba * normalize(woba_2h, lower_is_better = TRUE),

      season_part = BULLPEN_WEIGHTS$k_bb * k_bb_score +
                    BULLPEN_WEIGHTS$hr   * hr_score +
                    BULLPEN_WEIGHTS$woba * woba_score,

      composite = ifelse(
        is.na(second_half_score),
        season_part / (1 - BULLPEN_WEIGHTS$second_half),
        season_part + BULLPEN_WEIGHTS$second_half * second_half_score
      )
    ) %>%
    select(-season_part) %>%
    arrange(team, desc(composite))
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Team bullpen score = average of that team's listed arms
# ------------------------------------------------------------
get_team_bullpen_scores <- function(scores_df) {
  scores_df %>%
    group_by(team) %>%
    summarise(bullpen_score = mean(composite, na.rm = TRUE),
              n_arms = sum(!is.na(composite)), .groups = "drop") %>%
    arrange(desc(bullpen_score))
}
```

```{r}
# ============================================================
# team_composites.R
# Rolls each module's per-player scores up into ONE score per team
# per section: rotation, lineup, defense, bullpen.
#
# Rotation: top 3 starters x2, 4th x1        (full = /7) -- from your picked rotations
# Lineup:   top 7 hitters  x1.5, rest x1     (full 11 = /14.5)
# Bullpen:  top 4 arms     x2, rest x1       (full 7 = /11)
# Defense:  team composite as-is
#
# "Top" = highest composite within the team. Divides by the sum of
# weights actually used, so a player with missing data doesn't count
# as a zero.
#
# Takes the ALREADY-BUILT data frames as inputs -- build each module
# first, then call this. (Don't re-source all four scripts and then
# rebuild: they each define their own WEIGHTS/normalize(), so the
# last one sourced overwrites the others.)
# ============================================================

library(dplyr)

TEAM_ALIASES <- c("TB" = "TBR", "SD" = "SDP", "CWS" = "CHW", "WSH" = "WSN",
                  "KC" = "KCR", "SF" = "SFG", "AZ" = "ARI")
normalize_team <- function(x) {
  x <- toupper(trimws(x))
  ifelse(x %in% names(TEAM_ALIASES), TEAM_ALIASES[x], x)
}

# Weighted average of one team's scores: sort high->low, first
# `top_n` get `top_w`, everyone else gets 1.
weighted_top <- function(scores, top_n, top_w) {
  s <- sort(scores, decreasing = TRUE, na.last = TRUE)
  w <- ifelse(seq_along(s) <= top_n, top_w, 1)
  ok <- !is.na(s)
  sum(w[ok] * s[ok]) / sum(w[ok])
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Rotation: takes your already-picked rotations (the get_team_rotation()
# results with only_players), stacked into one data frame:
#   rotations <- bind_rows(PHI_rotation, LAD_rotation, ...)
# ------------------------------------------------------------
team_rotation_scores <- function(rotations, top_n = 3, top_w = 2) {
  rotations %>%
    mutate(team = normalize_team(team)) %>%
    group_by(team) %>%
    summarise(rotation = weighted_top(composite, top_n, top_w), .groups = "drop")
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Lineup / bullpen: same idea, different weights
# ------------------------------------------------------------
team_lineup_scores <- function(lineup_scores, top_n = 7, top_w = 1.5) {
  lineup_scores %>%
    mutate(team = normalize_team(team)) %>%
    group_by(team) %>%
    summarise(lineup = weighted_top(composite, top_n, top_w), .groups = "drop")
}

team_bullpen_scores <- function(bullpen_scores, top_n = 4, top_w = 2) {
  bullpen_scores %>%
    mutate(team = normalize_team(team)) %>%
    group_by(team) %>%
    summarise(bullpen = weighted_top(composite, top_n, top_w), .groups = "drop")
}

team_defense_scores <- function(defense_scores) {
  defense_scores %>%
    transmute(team = normalize_team(team), defense = composite)
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# All four side by side, one row per playoff team
# ------------------------------------------------------------
build_team_composites <- function(rotations = pitching_scores, lineup = lineup_scores,
                                  defense = defense_scores, bullpen = bullpen_scores) {
  teams <- unique(normalize_team(lineup_scores$team))

  team_lineup_scores(lineup_scores) %>%
    full_join(team_rotation_scores(rotations),             by = "team") %>%
    full_join(team_defense_scores(defense_scores),         by = "team") %>%
    full_join(team_bullpen_scores(bullpen_scores),         by = "team") %>%
    filter(team %in% teams) %>%
    select(team, rotation, lineup, defense, bullpen)
}

# Example:
# rotations <- bind_rows(PHI_rotation, LAD_rotation, ...)  # your picked rotations
# lineup    <- build_lineup_scores(2026, "2026-07-01", "2026-10-01")
# defense   <- build_team_defense_scores()
# pen       <- build_bullpen_scores()
# teams_df  <- build_team_composites(rotations, lineup, defense, pen)
```

```{r}
# ============================================================
# predict_series.R
# Fills the Predictions column of the submission template:
# P(BetterSeed wins a best-of-SeriesLength series).
#
# Steps:
#  1. Team section scores (rotation, lineup, defense, bullpen) from
#     team_composites.R are z-scored across the playoff field, so each
#     section's weight means what it says regardless of its raw spread.
#  2. Per series length, weight the sections into one team rating
#     (ROUND_WEIGHTS), then re-standardize.
#  3. Bradley-Terry single game: P(win) = logistic(GAME_SCALE * gap +/- HFA)
#  4. Walk through the actual home/away schedule of the series
#     (3: all at better seed; 5: 2-2-1; 7: 2-3-2) to get P(series).
#
# Brier score rewards calibration: MLB series are close to coin flips,
# so GAME_SCALE is deliberately modest.
# ============================================================

library(dplyr)

# ---- Section weights per series length (EDIT THESE) --------
# Same split for every series length for now -- change a row to
# weight a round differently.
ROUND_WEIGHTS <- list(
  "3" = c(rotation = 0.30, lineup = 0.40, defense = 0.10, bullpen = 0.20),
  "5" = c(rotation = 0.30, lineup = 0.40, defense = 0.10, bullpen = 0.20),
  "7" = c(rotation = 0.30, lineup = 0.40, defense = 0.10, bullpen = 0.20)
)

# ---- Model scale -------------------------------------------
# GAME_SCALE: logit change per 1 SD of team rating. At 0.15:
#   gap (SD)   best-of-3   best-of-5   best-of-7   (incl. home field)
#     0          0.55        0.51        0.51
#     1          0.60        0.58        0.59
#     2          0.65        0.65        0.67
#     3          0.70        0.71        0.74
# i.e. the best-vs-worst playoff matchup tops out around 70-75%,
# which is about as confident as MLB series history supports.
GAME_SCALE <- 0.15
# HFA_LOGIT: home-field edge; 0.12 ~= home team wins 53% (postseason-ish)
HFA_LOGIT  <- 0.12

# 1 = game at the better seed's park
HOME_PATTERNS <- list(
  "3" = c(1, 1, 1),
  "5" = c(1, 1, 0, 0, 1),
  "7" = c(1, 1, 0, 0, 0, 1, 1)
)

# MLB official team IDs -> the team codes used in the other CSVs
MLB_ID_TO_CODE <- c(
  "108" = "LAA", "109" = "ARI", "110" = "BAL", "111" = "BOS", "112" = "CHC",
  "113" = "CIN", "114" = "CLE", "115" = "COL", "116" = "DET", "117" = "HOU",
  "118" = "KCR", "119" = "LAD", "120" = "WSN", "121" = "NYM", "133" = "ATH",
  "134" = "PIT", "135" = "SDP", "136" = "SEA", "137" = "SFG", "138" = "STL",
  "139" = "TBR", "140" = "TEX", "141" = "TOR", "142" = "MIN", "143" = "PHI",
  "144" = "ATL", "145" = "CHW", "146" = "MIA", "147" = "NYY", "158" = "MIL",
  "35"  = "SDP"   # template's ID for the Padres (typo for 135) -- kept as-is in output
)

zscore <- function(x) (x - mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)) / sd(x, na.rm = TRUE)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Team rating for a given series length
# ------------------------------------------------------------
team_ratings <- function(teams_df, series_length) {
  w <- ROUND_WEIGHTS[[as.character(series_length)]]
  z <- teams_df %>%
    mutate(across(c(rotation, lineup, defense, bullpen), zscore))

  z %>%
    mutate(rating = w["rotation"] * rotation + w["lineup"]  * lineup +
                    w["defense"]  * defense  + w["bullpen"] * bullpen,
           rating = zscore(rating)) %>%
    select(team, rating)
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# P(better seed wins series), following the real home/away order
# ------------------------------------------------------------
series_win_prob <- function(r_better, r_worse, series_length) {
  gap    <- GAME_SCALE * (r_better - r_worse)
  p_home <- plogis(gap + HFA_LOGIT)
  p_away <- plogis(gap - HFA_LOGIT)
  need    <- (series_length + 1) / 2
  pattern <- HOME_PATTERNS[[as.character(series_length)]]

  f <- function(i, j) {
    if (i == need) return(1)
    if (j == need) return(0)
    p <- if (pattern[i + j + 1] == 1) p_home else p_away
    p * f(i + 1, j) + (1 - p) * f(i, j + 1)
  }
  f(0, 0)
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Fill the template and save
# ------------------------------------------------------------
fill_predictions <- function(teams_df, template_path, out_path = "predictions.csv") {
  tmpl <- read.csv(template_path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE, check.names = FALSE)

  # Excel-saved CSVs often carry blank trailing rows -- drop them
  tmpl <- tmpl[!is.na(tmpl$BetterSeedID) & !is.na(tmpl$WorseSeedID) &
                 !is.na(tmpl$SeriesLength), ]

  ids <- unique(as.character(c(tmpl$BetterSeedID, tmpl$WorseSeedID)))
  unknown_ids <- setdiff(ids, names(MLB_ID_TO_CODE))
  if (length(unknown_ids) > 0) {
    stop("Unrecognized team IDs in template: ", paste(unknown_ids, collapse = ", "))
  }

  tmpl$better_code <- unname(MLB_ID_TO_CODE[as.character(tmpl$BetterSeedID)])
  tmpl$worse_code  <- unname(MLB_ID_TO_CODE[as.character(tmpl$WorseSeedID)])

  missing <- setdiff(unique(c(tmpl$better_code, tmpl$worse_code)), teams_df$team)
  if (length(missing) > 0) {
    stop("No team scores for: ", paste(missing, collapse = ", "),
         " -- check team codes in teams_df.")
  }

  ratings <- lapply(c(3, 5, 7), function(L) team_ratings(teams_df, L))
  names(ratings) <- c("3", "5", "7")
  get_r <- function(code, L) {
    r <- ratings[[as.character(L)]]
    r$rating[r$team == code]
  }

  tmpl$Predictions <- mapply(function(b, w, L) {
    series_win_prob(get_r(b, L), get_r(w, L), L)
  }, tmpl$better_code, tmpl$worse_code, tmpl$SeriesLength)

  tmpl <- tmpl %>% select(-better_code, -worse_code)
  write.csv(tmpl, out_path, row.names = FALSE)
  message("Wrote ", nrow(tmpl), " rows to ", out_path,
          " | Predictions range: ",
          round(min(tmpl$Predictions), 3), " - ", round(max(tmpl$Predictions), 3))
  invisible(tmpl)
}

# Example:
# teams_df <- build_team_composites(rotations, lineup, defense, pen)
# preds    <- fill_predictions(teams_df, "submission_template.csv")
```
